title: Prevent Household Plumbing Leaks: Under-Sink Checks, Washer Pan, Hose Maintenance, and Pipe Insulation

summary: This Old House presents practical steps to prevent household plumbing leaks by teaching how to inspect common leak points under sinks and around appliances, mitigate washer-related flood risk with a plumbed catch pan and optional shut-off devices, recognize and prevent hose failures, and winterize exposed pipes with insulation. The host demonstrates visual leak indicators (moisture, bubbling, discoloration), discusses the limitations of catch pans, and covers proactive maintenance like hose replacement and installing moisture-sensing or manual shut-off solutions. The segment concludes with insulation techniques for unheated spaces to reduce freezing and subsequent bursting.

sections.title: Under-sink and appliance connection leak checks
sections.description: Inspect drain and supply lines for moisture, seal integrity, discoloration, and potential past leaks. Look for moisture at connections and signs of past water intrusion.

sections.title: Washer-leak risk and catch-pan recommendation
sections.description: In a finished space, place a drain-pan beneath the washing machine and ensure the pan has a path to drain to capture leaks.

sections.title: Hose failure prevention and pipe insulation
concepts: manual shut-off and auto shut-off options
sections.description: Discusses hose failure risks with examples, recommends hose replacement every 3-5 years, describes manual shut-offs and moisture-sensing devices, and covers insulating exposed pipes to prevent freezing and bursts.
